cemc-cayley-2009-04.title: Check the choices
cemc-cayley-2009-04.body:
Try $n = 44$: $\sqrt{5 + 44} = \sqrt{49} = 7$. ✓ (For example $n = 24$ gives $\sqrt{29}$, which is not 7.)

**Answer: (D) 44**

cemc-cayley-2009-05.title: Pythagorean triples
cemc-cayley-2009-05.body:
From the 3-4-5 triangle, $3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2$. From the 5-12-13 triangle, $5^2 + 12^2 = 13^2$. So the sum is $13^2$.

**Answer: (A) $13^2$**

cemc-cayley-2009-06.title: Fraction of the full turn
cemc-cayley-2009-06.body:
A sector with 20% of the area has 20% of the $360^\circ$ central angle: $x = \frac15 \cdot 360 = 72$.

**Answer: (D) 72**

cemc-cayley-2009-07.title: Isosceles triangle and right triangle
cemc-cayley-2009-07.body:
In right triangle $QSR$, $\angle SQR = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 65^\circ = 25^\circ$.
Since $PQ = PR$, $\angle PQR = \angle PRQ = 65^\circ$, so $x + 25 = 65$ and $x = 40$.

**Answer: (E) 40**

cemc-cayley-2009-07.title: Use triangle $PQS$
cemc-cayley-2009-07.body:
Since $PQ = PR$, $\angle PQR = 65^\circ$ and so $\angle QPR = 180^\circ - 130^\circ = 50^\circ$. In right triangle $PQS$, $x = 180 - 90 - 50 = 40$.

**Answer: (E) 40**

cemc-cayley-2009-08.title: Test an example
cemc-cayley-2009-08.body:
$1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 = 6$ is not odd and not a multiple of 4, 5 or 12. That rules out every choice except "a multiple of 6".

**Answer: (B) a multiple of 6**

cemc-cayley-2009-08.title: Why it always works
cemc-cayley-2009-08.body:
Among three consecutive integers at least one is even and exactly one is a multiple of 3, so the product is divisible by $2 \cdot 3 = 6$.

**Answer: (B) a multiple of 6**

cemc-cayley-2009-10.title: Multiply the three areas
cemc-cayley-2009-10.body:
Let the width, height and depth be $w, h, d$. Then $wh = 12$, $dh = 6$, $dw = 8$. Multiplying, $(whd)^2 = 12 \cdot 6 \cdot 8 = 576$, so the volume is $whd = \sqrt{576} = 24$.

**Answer: (A) 24**

cemc-cayley-2009-10.title: Find the dimensions
cemc-cayley-2009-10.body:
Try width 4, height 3, depth 2: front $4 \times 3 = 12$, side $2 \times 3 = 6$, top $4 \times 2 = 8$. ✓ Volume $= 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 = 24$.

**Answer: (A) 24**

cemc-cayley-2009-11.title: Use the short songs first
cemc-cayley-2009-11.body:
To play as many songs as possible, use the shortest ones first. All 50 three-minute songs take 150 minutes, leaving $180 - 150 = 30$ minutes for $30 \div 5 = 6$ five-minute songs. Total: $50 + 6 = 56$.

**Answer: (C) 56**

cemc-cayley-2009-12.title: Go down the last column
cemc-cayley-2009-12.body:
Each row has 6 boxes, so each number in the last column is $6 \times 3 = 18$ more than the one above it. $x$ is 5 rows below 17, so $x = 17 + 5 \cdot 18 = 107$.

**Answer: (C) 107**

cemc-cayley-2009-12.title: Count terms
cemc-cayley-2009-12.body:
The grid has 6 rows of 6, so $x$ is the 36th term of $2, 5, 8, \ldots$: $x = 2 + 35 \cdot 3 = 107$.

**Answer: (C) 107**

cemc-cayley-2009-13.title: Net movement
cemc-cayley-2009-13.body:
Count right as positive: $-1 + 2 - 3 + 4 - 5 + 6 = 3$. (Starting on square 8 of 15, the coin goes to 7, 9, 6, 10, 5, 11 — it never falls off.) It ends 3 squares to the right.

**Answer: (E) 3 squares to the right of where it started**

cemc-cayley-2009-14.title: Smallest possible sum
cemc-cayley-2009-14.body:
The smallest composites are 4, 6, 8, 9, ... so the sum of three different composites is at least $4 + 6 + 8 = 18$. The smallest prime that is at least 18 is 19, and indeed $19 = 4 + 6 + 9$.

**Answer: (D) 19**

cemc-cayley-2009-15.title: Build the list
cemc-cayley-2009-15.body:
In increasing order the list is $a, b, 9, d, e$. The 8 appears at least twice and is less than the median, so $a = b = 8$. The sum is $5 \times 10 = 50$, so $d + e = 50 - 25 = 25$. No other number repeats, so $10 \le d < e$. To make $e$ biggest, take $d = 10$, giving $e = 15$.

The list $8, 8, 9, 10, 15$ works.

**Answer: (A) 15**

cemc-cayley-2009-16.title: Use the left side two ways
cemc-cayley-2009-16.body:
The four small squares along the bottom have equal heights, so equal sides $x$; the large square above them has side $4x$. The right column of three shaded squares has height $30$, so $PS = 30$ too. Hence $4x + x = 30$, $x = 6$, and the largest square has side $4x = 24$.

**Answer: (B) 24**

cemc-cayley-2009-17.title: Maximize die by die
cemc-cayley-2009-17.body:
Opposite faces sum to 7, so whenever both faces of an opposite pair are visible they give 7; for the other visible faces we choose the largest numbers.

- The top die of the tallest column shows 5 faces: hide the 1, giving $2+3+4+5+6 = 20$.
- The two dice that show 3 faces (one opposite pair plus one more): $7 + 6 = 13$ each.
- The two dice that show 4 faces (one opposite pair plus two adjacent faces): $7 + 6 + 5 = 18$ each.
- The die that shows 2 faces shows an opposite pair: $7$.

Total: $20 + 13 + 13 + 18 + 18 + 7 = 89$ (and $5+3+3+4+4+2 = 21$ faces).

**Answer: (C) 89**

cemc-cayley-2009-18.title: Rise and run
cemc-cayley-2009-18.body:
$P$ is 6 above the $x$-axis. On the line of slope 1, a drop of 6 needs a run of 6, so $Q = (-5, 0)$. On the line of slope 2, a drop of 6 needs a run of 3, so $R = (-2, 0)$. Thus $QR = 3$ and the area is $\frac12 \cdot 3 \cdot 6 = 9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

cemc-cayley-2009-18.title: Equations of the lines
cemc-cayley-2009-18.body:
The lines are $y = x + 5$ and $y = 2x + 4$, with $x$-intercepts $-5$ and $-2$. The base is $3$, the height is $6$, so the area is $9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

cemc-cayley-2009-19.title: Complementary counting
cemc-cayley-2009-19.body:
The product is 0 exactly when some digit is 0. Among $5000$–$5999$ (numbers $5xyz$), those with no 0 have $9^3 = 729$ choices, so $1000 - 729 = 271$ contain a 0. Adding $6000$ gives $272$.

**Answer: (D) 272**

cemc-cayley-2009-20.title: Set up the time difference
cemc-cayley-2009-20.body:
Let the route be $d$ km. The two trip times differ by 2 minutes $= \frac{1}{30}$ h:
$$\frac{d}{70} - \frac{d}{75} = \frac{1}{30} \implies \frac{5d}{5250} = \frac{1}{30} \implies d = 35.$$

**Answer: (B) 35 km**

cemc-cayley-2009-20.title: Check the choices
cemc-cayley-2009-20.body:
For 35 km: at 70 km/h the trip takes 30 minutes, at 75 km/h it takes 28 minutes — a 2-minute difference, as needed.

**Answer: (B) 35 km**

cemc-cayley-2009-21.title: Bound the $x$-coordinate
cemc-cayley-2009-21.body:
The square has corners $(0,0)$ and $(2009,2009)$. Every integer $a$ gives the lattice point $(a, 3a - 5)$. We need $0 \le 3a - 5 \le 2009$, i.e. $\frac53 \le a \le \frac{2014}{3} = 671.\overline3$. So $2 \le a \le 671$, which is $670$ values (also $0 < a < 2009$ holds). From $(2, 1)$ to $(671, 2008)$ there are 670 lattice points.

**Answer: (E) 670**

cemc-cayley-2009-22.title: Substitute
cemc-cayley-2009-22.body:
Put $b = 3 - a$: the second equation becomes $ac - a = 15$, the third $3c - ac + a = 6$. Adding: $3c = 21$, $c = 7$.

**Answer: (E) 7**

cemc-cayley-2009-23.title: Pick a convenient total
cemc-cayley-2009-23.body:
Say the land is 100 hectares. Angela has 60, Barry 40. Corn covers 70 and peas 30 overall. Angela's corn is $\frac45 \cdot 60 = 48$ and her peas 12. So Barry has $70 - 48 = 22$ corn and $30 - 12 = 18$ peas: $22 : 18 = 11 : 9$.

**Answer: (A) 11 : 9**

cemc-cayley-2009-23.title: Fractions of the whole
cemc-cayley-2009-23.body:
Angela's corn is $\frac45 \cdot \frac35 = \frac{12}{25}$ of the land and her peas $\frac{3}{25}$. Barry's corn: $\frac{7}{10} - \frac{12}{25} = \frac{11}{50}$; peas: $\frac{3}{10} - \frac{3}{25} = \frac{9}{50}$. Ratio $11 : 9$.

**Answer: (A) 11 : 9**

cemc-cayley-2009-24.title: Midline and angle bisectors
cemc-cayley-2009-24.body:
Call the field $ABCD$ with long base $AD$, $AB = BC = CD = 100$ and base angles $60^\circ$. Since $60^\circ + 120^\circ = 180^\circ$, $BC \parallel AD$, so it is an isosceles trapezoid.

**Whole area.** Dropping perpendiculars from $B$ and $C$: each overhang is $100\cos 60^\circ = 50$ and the height is $100 \sin 60^\circ = 50\sqrt3$. So $AD = 200$ and the area is $\frac12(100 + 200)(50\sqrt3) = 7500\sqrt3$.

**Region closest to $AD$.** A point is closer to $AD$ than to $BC$ when it lies below the midline (height $25\sqrt3$). It is closer to $AD$ than to $AB$ when it lies below the bisector of $\angle A$ (points on an angle bisector are equidistant from the two sides), and similarly for $D$. The bisectors make $30^\circ$ with $AD$; they reach height $25\sqrt3$ at horizontal distance $25\sqrt3 \cdot \sqrt3 = 75$ from $A$ and from $D$. Since $75 + 75 < 200$, the region is a trapezoid with bases $200$ and $200 - 150 = 50$ and height $25\sqrt3$, of area $\frac12(200 + 50)(25\sqrt3) = 3125\sqrt3$.

**Fraction:** $\dfrac{3125\sqrt3}{7500\sqrt3} = \dfrac{5}{12}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{5}{12}$**

cemc-cayley-2009-25.title: Tiny unshaded corner triangles
cemc-cayley-2009-25.body:
Put the rectangle at $(0,0)$–$(m,n)$; the diagonal is $y = \frac{n}{m}x$ with slope between $\frac13$ and $\frac12$.

A partly shaded square is cut by the diagonal into (i) a shaded triangle — area at most $\frac12 \cdot 1 \cdot \frac12 = \frac14$; (ii) two trapezoids — the unshaded part is at least a triangle of base 1 and height $\ge \frac13$, area $\ge \frac16$; or (iii) a small **unshaded triangle** in the top-left corner. Only (iii) can give shaded area $> 0.999$.

Let the top-left corner be the lattice point $(p, q)$, below the line... i.e. just above it. The unshaded triangle has legs $\frac{m}{n}q - p$ (horizontal) and $q - \frac{n}{m}p$ (vertical), so its area is
$$\frac12\cdot\frac{(mq - np)^2}{mn}.$$
We need $0 < \frac{(mq - np)^2}{2mn} < 0.001$, i.e. $mn > 500(mq - np)^2 \ge 500$, since $mq - np$ is a nonzero integer. To get $mn$ as small as possible we want $mq - np = 1$ (so $\gcd(m, n) = 1$) and $mn > 500$ with $2n < m < 3n$.

Check $501$ to $510$: only $504 = 36 \cdot 14$ and $510 = 34 \cdot 15$ factor with $2n < m < 3n$. For $(36, 14)$, $36q - 14p$ is even, never 1. For $(34, 15)$, $34 \cdot 4 - 15 \cdot 9 = 1$ works. So the smallest value is $mn = 510$.

**Answer: (C) $506 \le mn \le 510$**
